title: Field-induced incipient spin-density phase stabilized inside the nematic phase of FeSe$_{1-x}$S$_x$
authors: I. Paulescu, R. M. Abedin, J. S. Pearce, W. H. Fong, Z. Zajicek, A. Morfoot, W. Knafo, O. Squire, D. Graf, A. A. Haghighirad, A. I. Coldea
abstract: Spin-density wave (SDW) order and superconductivity frequently compete and coexist in unconventional superconductors, where spin fluctuations often mediate superconducting pairing. In iron-chalcogenide superconductors, FeSe$_{1-x}$S$_x$, SDW order has only been detected under applied pressure, while both spin and nematic fluctuations are involved in determining their rich superconducting phase diagrams. Here, we report evidence for an incipient SDW phase, within the nematic state of FeSe$_{1-x}$S$_x$, revealed in magnetic fields up to 68~T. Once superconductivity is quenched, we observe sharp upturns in longitudinal resistivity accompanied by anomalies in tunnel diode oscillator frequency response and torque anisotropy, consistent with a field-induced electronic order. Dominant low-frequency quantum oscillations reveal a small reconstructed Fermi surface, consistent with a field-induced SDW order. Direct experimental comparisons with a pressure-tuned nematic, analogue, FeSe$_{0.96}$S$_{0.04}$, demonstrate that SDW phases are stabilized within the nematic phase of FeSe$_{1-x}$S$_x$ via both chemical substitution and applied pressure. These findings reveal that by weakening nematicity, the SDW orders are stabilised, which promotes the dominant superconducting pairing mechanism in iron chalcogenides.
summary: This work investigates the complex interplay between SDW order, nematicity, and superconductivity in FeSe1-xS_x. Using high-field magnetotransport and TDO measurements, the authors report finding an incipient SDW phase stabilized within the nematic state. This suggests that tuning or weakening nematicity is key to stabilizing the magnetic order that promotes superconductivity in these materials.
main_problem: Investigating the competition and coexistence between Spin-Density Wave (SDW) order and superconductivity (SC) in iron-chalcogenide superconductors, specifically focusing on the role of the nematic electronic state.
main_result: The study reports evidence for an incipient SDW phase stabilized within the nematic state of FeSe1-xS_x under high magnetic fields, suggesting that weakening nematicity promotes the dominant superconducting pairing mechanism.
method: The research employed magnetotransport measurements (resistivity, quantum oscillations), Tunnel Diode Oscillator (TDO) frequency response, and magnetic torque anisotropy measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the iron-chalcogenide superconductor FeSe1-xS_x, studied under varying conditions including chemical doping (x), applied hydrostatic pressure, and high magnetic fields (up to 68 T).
key_observables: Longitudinal resistivity upturns, TDO frequency anomalies, quantum oscillation frequencies (F), and magnetic torque anisotropy.
important_parameters: High magnetic fields (up to 68 T), chemical doping concentration (x), and applied pressure (p).
main_assumptions: The interpretation of resistivity upturns and TDO anomalies as definitive evidence for field-induced electronic order (SDW).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing the field-induced SDW phase in relation to doping and pressure, alongside transport and TDO behavior measurements demonstrating the SDW development.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes transport and TDO data across different doping levels and pressures, mapping out the phase boundaries where the field-induced SDW order emerges within the nematic superconducting state.
why_interesting: The interplay between competing electronic orders (SDW, nematicity, SC) in iron-based superconductors is a canonical problem in strongly correlated electron physics, providing experimental insights into pairing mechanisms.
